content:
View full tables and cross-tabulations of the results here.

Over the last week the L-NP Coalition has taken the lead on primary vote on 25.5% (up 3.5%): (22.5% Liberals, 3% Nationals) ahead of the ALP 24.5% (down 1%) and One Nation 23.5% (down 1%) for the first time since the 2025 Federal Election. Support for the Greens 14.5% (down 0.5%) and Independent/ Others 12% (down 1%) are both down slightly according to the Roy Morgan Poll conducted November 9-15, 2026, with a representative Australia-wide cross-section of 1,595 electors.

The L-NP Coalition now leads on a two-party preferred basis for the first time since the Federal Election: L-NP 52% (up 3% in a week) cf. ALP 48% (down 3%).

The L-NP has consistently improved its two-party preferred result for the last five weeks since early October.

When preferences for the major parties are allocated based on how Australians voted at the 2025 Federal Election the gap is closer, L-NP 50% (up 2.5%) cf. ALP 50% (down 2.5%). 

If a Federal Election were held now the result would likely be a narrow L-NP Coalition victory

In many electorates at the Federal Election the contest is set to be between the ALP and One Nation. When preferences are allocated for Coalition, Greens, Independent, and Other Party supporters between the ALP and One Nation, Roy Morgan estimates the ALP is in a stronger position and narrowly leads One Nation:
ALP 52.5% (down 1.5%) in front of One Nation 47.5% (up 1.5%).

ALP support down as Prime Minister Albanese attends Climate Change Summit in Türkiye 

Support for the ALP weakened in the week Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen, attended the United Nation’s Conference of the Parties (COP31) Climate Change Summit in Türkiye.

Prime Minister Albanese and Minister Bowen were caught discussing the impact of mobile phone radiation and joking about the impact of this radiation on their ‘private parts’.

Large majority of 64.5% of electors say Australia is ‘going in the wrong direction’ 

A large majority of Australians, 64.5% (down 1% from a week ago), say the country is ‘going in the wrong direction’. Only 21.5% (up 1%) say the country is ‘going in the right direction’.

Further details will be released in Roy Morgan’s weekly video update presented by Roy Morgan Chief Executive Officer Michele Levine.

For detailed analysis such as by States, capital cities/country areas, age, gender, occupation, and education contact Julian McCrann on (03) 9224 5365 or email julian.mccrann@roymorgan.com.

About Roy Morgan

Roy Morgan is Australia’s largest independent Australian research company, with offices in each state, as well as in the U.S. and U.K. A full-service research organisation, Roy Morgan has over 80 years’ experience collecting objective, independent information on consumers.

Roy Morgan Interviewing in September, October & November 2026: Primary Vote & Two-Party Preferred

*Interviewing dates of Australian electors aged 18+: Sep 14-27, 2026 (n=2,569), Sep. 28 – Oct 11, 2026 (n=2,655), Oct 12-25, 2026 (n=2,711), Oct 26 – Nov 8, 2026 (n=2,574), Nov 9-15, 2026 (n=1,595). This week 7.5% (up 1.5%) of those surveyed can’t say who they would vote for.
